recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit the remaining unreferenced profile-introduction stubs in core; future corrections to migrated profile definitions, CRMI-specific canonical URL handling, or CRMI explanatory text belong in the CRMI IG unless a later FHIR-core decision changes whether the logical patterns themselves should remain in the base specification.
issue_request: FHIR-38833 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I R5 request to move the Shareable/Publishable patterns and associated Shareable/Publishable profiles to the CRMI IG. The accepted resolution said the artifacts could not be removed before R5, so the applicable change was to add introductions on those profiles indicating they would move to CRMI and encouraging implementers to look there for updates, corrections, and clarifications.
initial_application: Jira records Git master 348dbf91cb. That commit added CRMI warning introductions for 20 Shareable, Publishable, Computable, and Executable profile pages; 885919d75b re-applied the notes as standalone profile-introduction files, and 80eecb02fa changed the CRMI link from build.fhir.org to the [%ig crmi%] macro. The profile-specific introduction files were later removed or left only as out-of-build stubs when the corresponding profile definitions were migrated out of core.
additional_context: Later applied issues govern the current source state. FHIR-48393 removed CDS/CQI profile definitions that had moved to CRMI or other IGs, and FHIR-37959 removed terminology-resource Shareable/Publishable/Computable/Executable profiles from core for R6 while maintaining them in CRMI. The combined branch already contains a FHIR-37959 no-change audit commit (d03c22085815adc28a5145788c36ffd231f07da2). CRMI issues FHIR-52711 and FHIR-52719 addressed the external CRMI URL and explanatory-text details for migrated terminology profiles. Current fhir.ini still builds the Shareable and Publishable logical patterns, but active [profiles] entries and resource implementation guides no longer include the migrated profile StructureDefinitions.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source change is needed because the original R5 warning text was applied, later final R6 decisions intentionally removed the profile definitions from current core build scope, and the current Shareable/Publishable pattern pages plus the Clinical Reasoning module already direct implementers to CRMI for the relevant content patterns, profiles, and guidance.
